question: What does the type-21/22 arm of the OptionTypeInfo apply (0x60bedc0) do on node #115, which entries can reach it, and what Status does each path return? Resolves #4311 open unknowns 1, 3 and 4.

apply.verification_4: Status OK immediately at 0x60bedeb; never parses (see #4311)
apply.custom_parse_dispatch: record+0x18 (parse manager) != 0: copy ConfigOptions, call *0x20(%rbp) with (Status*, record+0x8, config-copy, name, value, field-addr)

jump_table.entry_width: int32 relative offsets: movslq (%rcx,%rdx,4),%rdx; add %rcx,%rdx; jmp *%rdx (at 0x60bf050-0x60bf057)
jump_table.range_check: type > 0x18 bypasses the table: cmp $0x18; ja 0x60bf07e (at 0x60bf042-0x60bf045)
jump_table.types_17_20: fail the range test -> verification error path
jump_table.type_14: parse via 0x60be7f0, enum registry 0x6507020; on failure falls to 0x60bf078 -> 0x60bf07e -> verification error

apply.arm_is_primary: The arm is the PRIMARY parse for types 21/22 (jump-table direct dispatch), not a fallback after a failed primary parse; corrects #4311's phrasing. Whether a given entry reaches it depends on its parse function (see reachability).

flags_gate.any_set: 0x60bf418: deref field as pointer; value size == 0 -> Status OK; *(field) != 0 -> main body 0x60bf212; else kNotFound
flags_gate.none_set: 0x60bf20d: empty value -> Status OK, else main body 0x60bf212

steps: found -> 0x6099e70 (the '=' path); not found -> 0x609ba30 (the no-'=' path)

arm.error_outcome: The arm itself never synthesizes a verification error: a failure Status is whatever the callee returned, propagated verbatim. The only arm-level errors are the two kNotFound messages above.

flags_survey: Across all 214 mapped entries (#4237 DBOptions 100 + #4263 CFOptions 114), ONLY type-22 entries carry any of flags bits 0x200/0x400/0x800; none carries 0x800. The two apparent exceptions (prefix_extractor 0x1100, memtable_insert_with_hint_prefix_extractor 0x0) are pre-OR immediates: the type-22 helper forces 0x400 (or $0x4,%ch at 0x6083a99), so stored flags always have a bit set and the arm always derefs to the object pointer.
